expected.insightNarrative:
main page is the city factsheet of the Urban Audit city factsheets for 2019 Urban Adaptation Map Viewer, published by the European Environment Agency. A city is selected at the top; the dashboard shows Burgos, Spain, population 177,776, for the year 2014. The factsheet covers the city's observed and projected climate, its land cover and exposure to hazards, its socio-economic vulnerability and its adaptation activities, and lists the documents the figures come from. The story is a city with average heat and flood exposure, a rising forest fire danger and heavier summer downpours ahead, and no adaptation plan.

Key insights
- Flood exposure is stable: about 12% of all land uses are potentially exposed to a 1-in-100-year river flood, 12.35% in the 1961-1990 baseline and 11.92% projected for 2071-2100.
- The climate indicators with the highest values are 47.33 cooling degree days per year and a projected 22.41% increase in heavy summer precipitation by 2071-2100; forest fire danger is well above the average of other Urban Audit cities, and winter precipitation has fallen by 3.28 mm per decade.
- Burgos has no adaptation plan and has not signed the Covenant of Mayors on adaptation.

Observed and projected climate_Table (OK
A table of climate indicators for the city: 47.33 cooling degree days per year, 0.29 observed drought events per decade, a forest fire danger index of 3.65, 2.00 hot summer days per year, projected drought frequencies of 5.18 (2041-2070) and 10.78 (2071-2100) months per 30-year period, 13.00 projected extreme heatwaves, a projected forest fire danger of 4.35, 1.00 projected heatwave, a 22.41% projected change in heavy summer precipitation, a -0.82% projected change in heavy winter precipitation, 0.00 combined summer days and tropical nights, and observed trends of -1.30 mm per decade in summer precipitation and -3.28 mm per decade in winter precipitation.

CDD_0_1, SSR_0_1_OK, Prec_obs_win_0_1_OK, Obs_dr_0_1_OK
The city's climatic situation in relation to other Urban Audit cities, each shown on a scale from minimum to maximum: cooling degree days sit at the average, forest fire danger is well above average, winter precipitation has decreased, and droughts have increased.

green_0_1_OK
The city's rank in Europe on the share of green space in its Urban Morphological Zone: 19.03, close to the minimum.

2_% sealed surface in the city
The change in sealed surface from 2006 to 2015: about 50.58% of the Urban Morphological Zone and 18.65% of the core city, both nearly flat over the period.

3_% land uses UMZ potencially
Flood exposure: the share of land uses potentially exposed to a 1-in-100-year river flood, for the 1961-1990 baseline and for 2071-2100. All land uses stand at about 12%, transport at about 1%, residential at about 4% and commercial at about 3.5%, with almost no change between the two periods.

4_% city population
Forest fires 2000-2017: the share of the city's population, administrative area and land uses affected. Commercial land is the most affected at about 12%, the city area at about 5%, and population, residential and transport land are barely affected.

Vulnerability_table, Vulnerability_resume_onGrid, Vulnerability_resume_2
Socio-economic and demographic characteristics for 2014 and their position relative to other Urban Audit cities in Europe: children under 5 are 4.90% of the population (below average), people born in another country 8.00% (above average) and single pensioner households 10.6% (below average); there is no data for people 75 or older, the unemployment rate or lone parent households. According to the RAMSES project the city is in cluster 1, cities with low to medium vulnerability to heatwaves, droughts and floods. According to the RESIN project it belongs to the Southern Lands group, where water scarcity, wildfires and heat stress are becoming increasingly serious and landslides are an additional problem; cities of similar size in that group are listed.

City pop info, City pop info (2), City pop info (3)
The selected city's country (Spain), population (177,776) and reference year (2014).

Adaptation activities
Burgos does not have an adaptation plan and is not a signatory on adaptation to the Covenant of Mayors on Climate and Energy.

WebReferences
The list of source documents behind the figures: E-OBS, JRC, Met Office HadEX2, EURO-CORDEX, Copernicus, Eurostat, Tapia et al. (2017), RESIN and Reckien et al. (2018).
